_comment: Apollo CSM/LM/S-IVB mass, propulsion and inertia data. Values are rounded public figures for the Apollo 11 vehicle [published] or engineering estimates [estimated]; see README.md (Fidelity). Masses in kg, forces in N, lengths in m, inertia in kg*m^2.

mass._lm_source: LM-5 Eagle, 15,103 kg with full tanks [published]: the descent stage's dry mass and the propellant loads (dps, aps, lm_rcs) [published, rounded]; the ascent stage's dry mass, with the crew and their equipment, makes up the total [estimated]
mass._sivb_source: Apollo 11's vehicle at the second S-IVB ignition, 134,051 kg [published: AS-506 flight evaluation report, MPR-SAT-FE-69-9, Table 20-7], less the CSM and the LM here and the S-IVB's propellant (sivb): the S-IVB dry with the Instrument Unit, the adapter and the residuals, all left behind at transposition [derived]

sps._source: AJ10-137: 20,500 lbf vacuum thrust, Isp 314 s [published]

sm_rcs._source: R-4D, 100 lbf, Isp ~290 s; four quads [published]; usable load per quad [estimated]

cm_rcs._source: SE-8, 93 lbf, two independent rings [published]; load [estimated]

sivb._source: The J-2 in Apollo 11's second S-IVB burn, TLI: 894,364 N and 4,204 N s/kg at the standard time slice, and 61,151 kg of LOX with 13,301 kg of LH2 at the second ignition [published: AS-506 flight evaluation report, MPR-SAT-FE-69-9, Tables 7-2 and 7-3, best estimates; the thrust and the specific impulse held through the burn: simplified]

saturn_v._source: Apollo 11's Saturn V, AS-506, from the pad to parking orbit [published: AS-506 flight evaluation report, MPR-SAT-FE-69-9, unless marked]. liftoff_kg: at holddown arm release (Table 20-9). Each stage burns until its propellant is gone, the S-IVB's first burn until the IU's velocity cutoff; the masses at each stage's start are the report's (Table 20-9) and each stage's propellant its tanks' from start to cutoff (Tables 5-2 and 6-2).
saturn_v._cd_source: The axial force coefficient on the 10.06 m (33 ft) diameter against Mach, from the SA-506 flight manual's typical axial force and dynamic pressure through the S-IC's flight (MSFC-MAN-506, Figures 2-4 and 2-5) [derived]

s_ic._source: The F-1s: 6,719 kN and an Isp of 264.5 s each reduced to sea level (Table 5-1), 7,986 kN each in vacuum at OECO, 3.94 g on 827,292 kg (Tables 4-1 and 20-9); the thrust between them follows the air's pressure, on an exit area that lumps in the thrust's rise as the pumps' inlets pressurise [derived], and the Isp likewise from 264.5 s to 302 s, which empties the tanks, 2,074,429 kg from holddown release (Table 5-2), at the flown OECO [estimated]

s_ii._source: The second flight stage at the S-II's start command (Table 20-9) and its tanks' propellant from then to OECO (Table 6-2); five J-2s at the high mixture ratio, 5,141,516 N on 1,234.5 kg/s (Table 6-1), four after the centre engine's cutoff, and four at the low mixture ratio after the shift, 3,059,402 N (section 6) on the flow that burns the rest by the flown OECO [derived]; the aft interstage and the launch escape system jettisoned (Table 20-9)

s_ivb._source: The third flight stage at the S-IVB's first start command (Table 20-9); the J-2 in the first burn, 901,223 N on 214.38 kg/s (Table 7-1)

dps._source: Descent engine: 10,125 lbf full thrust, throttleable from 10 % to 60 % [published]; Isp and propellant load [published, rounded]; transients [estimated]. P40 starts it at 10 % for 15 s and then burns at 40 %, as Apollo 11's DOI did [published]

aps._source: Ascent engine: 3,500 lbf, fixed thrust [published]; Isp and propellant load [published, rounded]; transients [estimated]

lm_rcs._source: R-4D, 100 lbf, Isp ~290 s; sixteen jets in four quads on the ascent stage, fed by two systems, A and B, 633 lb of propellant in all [published]; the jets each system fires per axis and their lever arms [estimated]

descent_guidance._source: The LGC's powered-descent targets, in a frame at the landing site: x up, y crossrange, z downrange (m, m/s, m/s², m/s³). Designed for this simulator [estimated] after Klumpp's Apollo lunar descent guidance (MIT Draper Laboratory, 1971): a quadratic acceleration to each target, the time to go set by its downrange jerk. The approach phase's reference starts at high gate, 2,100 m up and 7 km out at 35 m/s down and 100 m/s downrange, and hands over to P65 10 s before its target at 40 m. Powered descent starts 470 km (ground range) before the site, with 26 s at 10 % throttle, and lasts about 730 s

lm_gear._source: The LM on its landing gear: its centre of mass above the footpads, and the contact probes 5.6 ft below them [published]; the landing's speed limits for the gear [estimated]

landing_radar._source: The LM's landing radar and the LGC's use of it. Antenna position 1 tilts the beam from the LM's -X axis toward -Z [estimated]; position 2 is along -X. The altitude beam's range, about 41,000 ft, and the velocity beams', about 33,000 ft [estimated from Apollo 11's acquisition near 37,000 ft]. The LGC reads the radar every 2 s [published] and weights its altitude and velocity into the state vector [estimated weights]

ascent_guidance._source: The LGC's powered ascent (P12). Insertion 60,000 ft above the landing site's radius, climbing at 32 ft/s [published: Apollo 11 shut down at 60,666 ft and 32.8 ft/s], with the horizontal velocity (about 5,535 ft/s) that puts apolune 45 nmi above the site, a 9 x 45 nmi orbit [estimated: Apollo 11 planned about 45 nmi and reached 47.3 by 9.5]. The vertical rise lasts until the LM climbs at 40 ft/s, the steering is held for the last 2 s, and the pitchover's rate is 10 deg/s [estimated]

rendezvous_radar._source: The LM's rendezvous radar, tracking the CSM's transponder out to 400 nmi [published]

lgc_executive._source: The LGC's load in the powered descent (src/systems/lgc_executive.gd, slice 9b). The computer ran at about 90 percent of its capacity at the descent's peak (Apollo 11 Mission Report, MSC-00171, section 16.2) [published]; the shares below are [estimated] to add up to it: 0.12 for the interrupts, and the Servicer's share falling from P63 to P66, with the landing radar's reading, P64's landing point designator job and a noun monitored by the crew with V16 on top (Luminary 1A's N68, the range, time to go and delta-H, dearer than the others, as Apollo 11's crew found). Their priorities are [estimated] in the order the model needs: the crew's monitor lowest. With the rendezvous radar's mode switch at AUTO TRACK or SLEW, its two coupling data units sent the LGC counter pulses of 11.7 microseconds each, 6,400 a second each at most (ibid.) [published]; they took about 13 percent of Apollo 11's LGC (Eyles, 2004) [published], 11,100 a second [derived]

rendezvous_guidance._source: The LGC's rendezvous programs. TPI when the CSM stands 26.6 deg above the LM's horizontal, and a transfer that meets it after it has flown 130 deg [published]. P20's radar marks come every 60 s. The first after the CSM's state vector arrives takes the radar's relative position outright; later marks weight it by 0.5, move the velocity by 0.15 of the position's residual per mark interval, and weight the range rate along the line of sight by 0.5. P35 aims its correction 5 min ahead [estimated]

lm_eps._source: The LM's batteries and load (src/systems/lm_eps.gd): the descent stage's four batteries' 1,600 A-h and the ascent stage's two's 592 A-h [published: MSC-02680, section 6.2]; its load powered down, 12 A, and powered up with the PGNS, 30 A at 900 W, Apollo 13's (ibid., sections 6.2 and 7.2.5) [published], the PGNS's the difference [derived]; the AGS's [estimated]

cm_lm._source: Apollo 13's command module and LM after the SM's jettison: 37,109.7 lb, 24,048, 92,418 and 93,809 slug ft2 about their X, Y and Z axes (MSC-02680, Table A-I) [published]; the CM's jets' arms [estimated: the CM's own]

unmodelled._source: Small forces on the CSM that its computer's navigation doesn't model [estimated]: the SM's vents (waste water, fuel cell purges) as a steady force, standard deviation per body axis in N (0.01 N is about 6e-7 m/s^2 on the CSM alone); and the attitude jets' net force from their mismatched thrust and alignment, standard deviation per body axis as a fraction of the force the jets' torque takes. Drawn once for the flight from the mission's seed (mission.json "dispersions")

imu._source: The CMC's IMU [estimated]: each gyro's drift about its stable member axis, standard deviation in deg/h (0.015 deg/h is one milli-earth-rate unit, within the Apollo IMU's specification), drawn once for the flight from the mission's seed (mission.json "dispersions"); and a coarse align's error about each axis, standard deviation in deg, drawn at each coarse align

docking._source: Probe-and-drogue docking [estimated throughout]: each docking port's distance from its vehicle's centre of mass along +X (the LM's, whole and as its ascent stage), the probe's push apart at undocking, the capture limits (closing speed, lateral speed, lateral miss, misalignment, relative rate), the radius within which the probe strikes the LM, and the rebound of a contact without capture. The docking tunnel's push at LM JETT from the CM: Apollo 13's command module, 12,367.6 lb after it, sensed 1.54, 0.42 and 1.00 ft/s in its axes, 1.88 ft/s (MSC-02680, section 6.4.1 and Table A-I) [published], the impulse that gives it along the docking axis [derived]

cm_aero._source: Hypersonic trim CD ~1.29, L/D ~0.30 on 3.91 m diameter [published, rounded]. The entry DAP's roll: at most 20 deg/s, the CM's roll acceleration on two jets 9.1 deg/s^2 (Comanche 055's CM entry DAP constants VM and A) [published]

els._source: Two 16.5 ft drogues at 24,000 ft, three 83.5 ft mains at 10,000 ft [published]; CdS [estimated]
